preamble: The retroflex fricative [ʂ] loses its retroflexion and becomes the alveolar fricative [s] in several unrelated languages. In Polish dialects with mazurzenie (Masovia, Masuria, most of Lesser Poland, parts of Silesia), standard sz [ʂ] corresponds to s [s], so sześć 'six' is [sɛɕt͡ɕ] and szyty 'sewn' becomes homophonous with syty 'full'. Its origin is debated: Koneczna derives it directly from the 16th-century depalatalization of the older palato-alveolars /ʃ, ʒ, t͡ʃ, d͡ʒ/, which gave retroflexes elsewhere but dentals here, while Kuryłowicz argues that archaic dialects adopted the new retroflexes and replaced them with dentals. It is treated here as a synchronic dialect correspondence of standard Polish retroflex cz, sz, ż, dż [t͡ʂ ʂ ʐ d͡ʐ] to mazurating c, s, z, dz.

Georgian merged the subscript-1 sibilant with plain *s, while Zan and Svan have š. Wiktionary's subscript-1 series (*s₁, *z₁, *c₁, *ʒ₁) is the Gamkrelidze-Machavariani 'hissing-hushing' series, given in the Wikipedia Proto-Kartvelian consonant table (after Gamkrelidze 1966 and Fähnrich 2002) as retroflex [ʂ ʐ ʈ͡ʂ ɖ͡ʐ].
